_what: The operating point: the one server command line every measurement and every instruction has to agree with.
_why: It was spelled out in three places that disagreed. On 2026-08-10 the vault page was missing --slot-save-path and --moe-stream-l2 32, while README.md and install.ps1 carried them. Nobody had changed anything wrongly; the copies simply drifted, and a measurement taken against the older line is not comparable to one taken against the newer.
_how_this_is_checked: tools/check_operating_point.py reads the RAW text of README.md and install.ps1 and extracts the flags from it. It must never read a second copy of this file - a checker that compares a manifest against itself is green forever.
_source_of_truth: This file. README.md and install.ps1 are renderings of it for humans; the measurement scripts take their defaults from it.

model._note: Not part of the install: 84.6 GiB and somebody else's artefact. 327,614,463 B per expert across 43 layers, read from the tensor tables of all three shards and confirmed by the server's own line (18,121.38 MiB / 58 slots = 312.44 MiB). model._why_this_rung: Moved from UD-IQ3_XXS on 2026-08-12, #89. Measured against it on the ten-task gate, three graded runs per rung, own server per run: 30/30 correct against 30/30, and the single deviation (two-sum, iq2-r2, DOES NOT RUN) is the extractor dropping an import placed above the function, not the model -- the answer was complete and correct. Throughput on the same tasks: decode 18.63 -> 19.53 tok/s (+4.8 %), ms per miss 0.7097 -> 0.6470 (-8.8 %), VRAM after load 31,074 -> 27,994 MiB. Prefill on a 1,884-token prompt 118.26 -> 133.10 (+12.6 %). The mechanism is bytes per miss, not cache slots: the hit rate moved 0.11 points across a 13.38 % smaller slab.
model._what_is_not_measured_on_this_rung: The slot ladder (56/58/60/62/64) and the host-tier pairing were measured on UD-IQ3_XXS and have NOT been repeated here. 58 slots is carried over unchanged, which is safe rather than optimal: the smaller slab leaves about 4.6 GB of card free after load against IQ3's 2.0 GB, so a larger cache would fit -- but 0731 covers 95 % of selections in 9.0 % of experts and 58 slots is already 2.5x past that, so more slots buy nothing measurable. Also unmeasured on this rung: the vendor KLD gap (0.30789 -> 0.48487, top-1 81.93 % -> 76.60 %) against anything other than ten algorithmic tasks.

models._what: Every GGUF a measurement script may point at, by key. tools/model-paths.ps1 reads this; nothing else spells a model path out.
models._why: Measured 2026-08-10: 26 lines across 18 files carried a model path, and 22 of those 26 pointed at files that no longer exist. Not one script was broken by it -- they all take -Model as a parameter, so the dead path is a default nobody notices until a run silently measures the wrong thing, or a model switch has to find 18 files.
models._root_is_resolved_at_runtime: NO `_root` SHIPS (#196 C1). The tree the entries resolve under is crow_platform.models_dir(): $CROW_MODELS if set, else <install>/models. A measurement machine whose tree lives elsewhere sets CROW_MODELS to it; model_candidates tries every entry path as written and as its basename, so a lab tree and an install both resolve. A `_root` written into a manifest is still honoured first (tests use it), but the shipped file carries none: a profile path in here named one person's machine on every install.

flash-next-q2-k-xl._reasoning_budget_note: MEASURED 2026-08-31 (#176) against the shipped operating point (pin 6c84c7d5d + PR #27992, port 8083), one server for the whole series, one prompt, n=3 per arm, paired by seed so that what differs inside a repetition can only be the cap. WITHOUT a cap: 7870 reasoning tokens against 4432 answer tokens, 61.6 percent share, 352.0 s. WITH one: 1024 -> 116.3 s, 512 -> 124.5 s, 256 -> 123.5 s. So capping AT ALL is worth about 2.8x wall clock, paired 3/3 against the uncapped arm in every repetition. WHERE the cap sits is NOT measurable: 116.3 / 124.5 / 123.5 s, and the spread inside each arm is far larger than the differences between them. 1024 is the entry rather than 256 for exactly that reason -- at an indistinguishable cost it removes the least thinking, which is the only axis on which the three still differ. THE CAP NEVER TRAVELS ALONE: the server's --reasoning-budget-message defaults to none (common/arg.cpp:3728), so the thinking block is force-closed and the model keeps writing where it stood -- 2 of 9 capped answers arrived mid-word, one of them continuing the split word `chat/` + `tokens`. With cli/crow_core.py's REASONING_BUDGET_MESSAGE it was 0 of 6 on the same seeds, and 185.1 s down to 80.8 s, because the cut answers were also the runaway ones. NOT MEASURED: answer QUALITY under a cap. Structure was judged -- does the answer begin as an answer -- and correctness was not, and no goal run has been repeated with the cap in place. NOT MEASURED on any other model, whose entries therefore declare no budget and keep the uncapped behaviour every release up to today shipped. MEASURED AGAIN THE SAME EVENING, in goal mode and with the cap wired in, on reasoning_effort high -- the level that thinks MOST. The largest single reasoning block of a whole ten-round goal run was 181 tokens; the ten blocks together were 676, counted through /tokenize and not estimated. The 1024 cap therefore never fired once, and REASONING_BUDGET_MESSAGE appears nowhere in that chat's archive (control: reasoning IS archived, ten blocks for ten rounds, none missing). SO THIS ENTRY SAVES NOTHING IN GOAL MODE. The 2.8x above was measured on a SINGLE prompt that produced ONE 7870-token block, and a per-request cap cannot touch a share that is a sum of many small blocks -- which is exactly what #176's 65-87 percent is. What this cap IS, is a brake on one runaway block in an ordinary chat turn, and that is where it was measured. Biting in goal mode would need something near 128; that is unmeasured, and at that size it would fire in nearly every round, which makes the unmeasured quality question the deciding one rather than a footnote. MEASURED A THIRD TIME the same evening, and this one decides the NUMBER. Four goal runs, interleaved off/128/off/128 on high, with folder, .crow/MEMORY.md, approvals.json and the goal reset before each: wall clock off 71.0 s and 59.8 s against capped 59.6 s and 88.0 s -- means 65.4 s against 73.8 s, and the two paired differences point in OPPOSITE directions (-11.4 s, +28.2 s), which is what no effect looks like. Reasoning totals tell the same story the other way round: off 917 and 658 tokens, capped 834 and 1178, so the CAPPED arm thought more. The run in which the cap fired four times needed 15 rounds and 17 tool calls against 10-12 rounds and 13-15 calls in the others -- the mechanism the reasoning level already showed on 2026-08-31: take the notepad away and the model replaces thinking with tool calls, and the extra rounds give back what the cap saved. THAT IS WHY THIS ENTRY IS 1024 AND NOT LOWER. Across all four runs the largest uncapped block was 324 tokens, so 1024 never fires in goal mode and cannot cost anything there; it exists for the single runaway block measured in an ordinary chat turn (7870 tokens, 352 s to 120 s, paired 3/3). 128 fires constantly and costs. Anyone lowering this number is re-running an experiment that has been run.

flash-next-q2-k-xl._reasoning_groups_note: MEASURED 2026-08-30 (#160), same probe as the levels note. UNSET (the key absent, which is what Crow sends for off) and high render BYTE-IDENTICALLY -- sha256 1be9942ae3ae, 299 chars -- so on this model off IS high, the same shape #117 measured for the 27B. low 9c5b77752e84 (228) and medium 53c9e1a9cf6e (90) are distinct. flash-next-cnq45-m._reasoning_levels_note: MEASURED 2026-09-18 (crow-nest #74) against `serve` on port 8099, the engine that opens this container. ACCEPTED: none, low, medium, high, xhigh. THE MAPPING IS THE ENGINE'S AND IT IS NOT llama-server's: this container carries the model's ORIGINAL template, which accepts xhigh, medium and low, defaults to xhigh and raises on anything else, so serve maps none -> thinking off, low and medium straight through, high and xhigh -> xhigh (crow-nest serve.rs map_reasoning_effort, its architecture 7.11.20). THE DOOR: crow-nest reads the TOP-LEVEL reasoning_effort and chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort, top level first, so the field this client has sent since #176 is the one that works -- before #74 it read neither and 758 of 758 [chat] lines of a live session reported reasoning chunks 0.
flash-next-cnq45-m._reasoning_groups_note: MEASURED 2026-09-18 (crow-nest #74) against serve on 8099, the same four messages every time (system, user, an assistant turn carrying reasoning_content, user), only reasoning_effort varied, temperature 0 and max_tokens 48 so the generation is a function of the prompt alone. Rendered prompt length from usage.prompt_tokens: off (key absent) 61, none 61, medium 59, low 85, high 97, xhigh 97 -- and the grouping is not the count alone: off/none and high/xhigh also produced the SAME 48 greedy tokens, character for character, which two different prompts do not. FOUR DISTINCT STEPS FOR SIX WORDS. OFF IS none HERE, NOT high, and that is the one place this entry differs from flash-next-q2-k-xl above: crow-nest renders enable_thinking false for a request that names no level, so the absent key is the NON-THINKING prompt rather than the template's xhigh default. On this engine an Off row is honest under the name none, and it is the CHEAPEST setting instead of the dearest -- the exact opposite of the trap #117 found on the 27B. servers._what: One server command line per model key. The keys are the keys of models.entries above, so a line and the GGUF it starts are named by the same word.
servers._why: A second model brings a second command line, and until #111 the checker took the FIRST region of a file that matched and never looked at the rest -- so the second line would have been unchecked prose sitting next to a checked one, which is the exact shape the whole manifest exists to prevent. Now every key here must find its own matching region in README.md and install.ps1, and a failure names the key.
servers._how_the_keys_stay_apart: NOT by order, and not by the port alone. Each entry declares only the flags its line carries, and a region satisfies a key only if it carries ALL of them: the 0731 line has --moe-stream and --chat-template-file and no -ctk, the Qwen line has -ctk/-ctv q8_0 and neither of the other two. Neither region can satisfy the other's key. If a future pair of models ever declares the same flag set, they must differ in some flag or the checker cannot tell which line it found.

operating-point._moe_stream_cache_note: 58 and not 64, measured 2026-08-11 (#87, evidence on #86). A slot costs 360.69 MiB - the server prints the cache size at every step and the figure is constant to five digits. The ladder, with the number of runs behind each cell, VRAM read after load out of 32,607 MiB: 64 -> prefill 15.28 median of 8 with spread 8.69x, no 200-token decode series taken, 32,014 used / 593 free; 62 -> prefill 114.92 median of 5, decode 14.62 median of 4 with one request at 7.07, 31,683 / 924; 60 -> 113.53 median of 5, 17.43 median of 8, 30,954 / 1,653; 58 -> 112.69 median of 3, 17.32 median of 8, 30,548 / 2,059; 56 -> 110.30 median of 3, 17.09 median of 8, 29,842 / 2,765. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE EVIDENCE: 62 reads 31,683 and 60 reads 30,954, i.e. 729 MiB for two slots against the 721 the printed slot size predicts, so 64 must read about 32,404 - and it reads 32,014. Those 390 MiB are what the driver moved to host memory without printing anything, and the affected request then halves with identical graph executions, identical misses and the LOWEST load stall of its run. 58 against 60 is NOT a throughput difference (112.69 vs 113.53, 17.32 vs 17.43, while repeating one configuration eight times spans 1.09x) - what separates them is the margin. CAUTION ON READING THE LADDER AS ONE SERIES: 58 and 56 were taken in one session and 62 and 60 in another, and a VRAM reading always contains whatever else was on the card at that moment. THE VALUE IS THIS CARD'S, NOT A CONSTANT: derived from 32,607 MiB of VRAM and whatever the display holds beside it.

qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_mmproj: MEASURED 2026-08-27 (#142). The model is a vision model and ran blind from day one: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF ships mmproj-F16.gguf (927,607,488 B), and without the flag /props says modalities.vision false. Measured with it against the same 27,730-token prompt, 3 runs each, cold cache: prefill 2,864.36 -> 2,849.41 tok/s (-0.5 %, inside both spreads), VRAM after load 27,991 -> 29,115 MiB, so the projector holds 1,124 MiB. One image costs (w/32)*(h/32) tokens after llama.cpp's smart-resize plus 2 markers, hard-capped at 4,096 = 2.0 % of the window -- measured on six images, zero deviation from the formula. The value is a path relative to the model roots, like models.entries.path, because the projector sits beside its GGUF in both trees. A model whose line has no mmproj key is text-only BY DESIGN, not by omission; a declared projector missing on disk boots text-only with a sentence (start_server), never silently. F16 over BF16: same size to 0.4 %, and F16 is the variant this machine measured. Raw runs: crow-lab/runs/2026-08-27-vision/.
qwen35-q4-k-xl._why_spec_type: MEASURED 2026-08-21, and it is the largest single win this model has produced. The GGUF ships its own multi-token-prediction head -- nextn_predict_layers = 1, tensors blk.64.nextn.eh_proj / enorm / hnorm / shared_head_norm -- and the command line left it idle until this date. Same prompt, same file, cold server, reasoning high: decode 123.05 tok/s against 66.51 without the flag on the tool-heavy prompt, 133.18 against 64.50 on the warm follow-up. Client and server agree to the digit -- the eleven eval-time blocks sum to 53.564 s for 6,591 tokens, and the eleven prompt-eval lines to 20,490. THE MECHANISM IS NOT FREE MULTIPLICATION: drafting costs 37 % of the pass rate, 65 main-model passes per second down to 41, and pays it back through 2.98 accepted tokens per pass. Acceptance over the turn was 4,379 of 6,630 drafted, 66 %, and per round it ran from 52 % on the big file-reading turn to 100 % on a short one. Quality was graded on the same run and is unchanged: every line number, the flag order and both format lines correct. NOT the same finding as 0731's, where a SEPARATE draft model costs 6 % because the streamed operating point pays in bytes -- this head lives inside the model and needs no second file. UNMEASURED: --spec-draft-n-max, which defaults to 3; at full acceptance the same 41 passes would carry 165 tok/s, so there is headroom nobody has looked at.

flash-next-q2-k-xl._why_binary: MAINLINE AT A PINNED COMMIT, PLUS TWO PATCHES -- AND THE SECOND WAS BELIEVED TO KILL THIS CARD UNTIL 2026-09-01. The tree is 6c84c7d5d (PR #27742, 'model: add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp)'), which is why the architecture no longer needs a fork. On top of it sit PR #28040 -- 'kv-cells: resolve get_prev_tokens in O(log n) from the sequence position index', ported by hand on 2026-09-01 (9 of 10 hunks, hunk 4 for_each_token_in -> seq_pos_tok_le placed manually, +40 -94 against the pin), replacing the draft #27992 that its own author closed the same day, measured at parity against it (fixed term +0.6 % against 1.335 ms of spread inside one arm; the closed PR's unit test ported across implementations: 9,480 lookups, 0 failures, and a deliberate off-by-one turns 3,416 of them red) -- and PR #27880 -- 'model: qwen4exp: reduce number of graph splits', MERGED upstream 2026-08-28 as 6fe749801, applied to the pin with ZERO hunks by hand: no commit between the pin and the PR's parent b387ddfd8 touches src/models/models.h or src/models/qwen4exp.cpp. The two patches are disjoint (#28040 is llama-kv-cache.cpp and llama-kv-cells.h, #27880 is models.h and qwen4exp.cpp), so against the #28040-only tree this line has exactly one variable. WHY #27880 WAS KEPT OUT UNTIL NOW, AND WHY THAT WAS WRONG: since 2026-08-30 this key said that b10687, one day younger than the pin, dies with 'ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed' during CUDA warmup, and that the only qwen4exp change between them is #27880. Both halves are true; the conclusion was not. The A/B was 6c84c7d5d against 6fe749801 -- a full day of mainline -- and the one log of such an abort that exists in crow-lab is runs/2026-08-30-mainline-qwen4exp/llama-server-8083.err.log (a wt-main build; it says 'ggml_cuda_compute_forward: MUL_MAT failed' at ggml-cuda.cu:107 right after the threadpool init, and carries no build number, so it is tied to b10687 by its date and tree, not by its own text; its sibling boot2.err.log of the same minute boots through; a search on 2026-09-01 had missed it). ISOLATED 2026-09-01 in crow-lab/wt-27880 = pin + #28040 + #27880: it boots, survives the full CUDA warmup, answers /health ok, and reports 62 graph splits per decoded token against 64 (92 against 94 at bs=2048) in every one of four boots. Whatever kills b10687 on this card lives in the rest of that day and is NOT attributed; the pin still does not move to b10687, but the reason is now 'unattributed', not '#27880'. The manifest's earlier explanation ('under -ncmoe those weights sit on the CPU') was wrong on its face: -ncmoe sets exactly LLM_FFN_EXPS_REGEX, which does not match ple_key or ple_value. A sharper, UNTESTED hypothesis is recorded in crow-lab/probe-27880.py: per_layer_token_embd.weight is 28,800,138,240 B and therefore read lazily off-card under --tensor-read-lazy auto, while token_embd sits on the card. WHAT #27880 IS WORTH HERE, MEASURED: it hoists the PLE embedding out of the per-layer loop into the token embedding's split, so it removes exactly the two PLE splits -- at -ncmoe 30 the other 60 of 64 are the CPU expert layers and stay. The '~52 tok/s if splits halve' arithmetic of the 2026-09-01 handover rested on a halving that does not happen at this placement. Four boots interleaved 28040/27880, six depths each, 200 new tokens, same unelevated shell, fits with r2 < 0.9 discarded (the first control cell ran on a busy machine -- prefill 193-422 tok/s against 555-737 everywhere else -- and is discarded on that evidence): fixed term 23.072 ms against 24.061 in the one clean pair = -0.989 ms (-4.1 %), slope +0.0076 per 1k, against 1.354 ms of spread inside the 27880 arm. Decode at the 30k depth 40.96 against 40.78 tok/s. Free and not worse; whether it is 1 ms better is below what two rounds resolve, and it was not chased further. THE ONLY OTHER LEVER LEFT INSIDE THE ENGINE IS DEAD, BY A DIRECT SWITCH: the same tree built with GGML_OPENMP=OFF -- ggml's own threadpool instead of vcomp140.dll, verified by the missing OPENMP field in system_info and GGML_OPENMP:BOOL=OFF in the cache -- costs +4 to +6 ms per token at 30k-140k depth in both rounds and pays a 42-70 ms first-request warm-up; --poll 100 on top is worse still. With OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE at -16.3 % from the same day, all three synchronizations available on this machine are measured and the default is the fastest. The 63.1 % of CPU time in barrier spin is the price of 24 hot threads at 62 handoffs per token, not a defect of the implementation. That number closed #186. Every layer that moves from CPU to GPU takes 10 x 1.7883 MiB = 17.9 MiB per token off the RAM bus and puts it on VRAM at ~20x the bandwidth. FENCED FROM BOTH SIDES, one variable each: -ncmoe 32 -> 59.6 s, -ncmoe 28 -> 97.5 s, -ub 1536 -> 55.5 s, -ub 3072 -> 98.8 s. It is an optimum, not a hit. STILL THE FLOOR: below -ncmoe 24 it spills into WDDM and prefill falls to ~27 tok/s. Neither a smaller ubatch (512 tried) nor a q4_0 KV cache moves that line -- it is the expert weights themselves, 24 layers on the GPU are ~22 GiB. sampling._what: What the client and every probe send when nobody says otherwise.
sampling._why: 1.0 / 0.95 is what DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 specifies. THE SOURCES DISAGREE and the disagreement belongs here rather than in anyone's memory: the model card (manifests/0731-encoding/model-card.md) runs its agentic benchmarks at temperature 1.0 with top_p 0.95; the model's own generation_config.json says temperature 1.0 with top_p 1.0. Crow is an agent, so the agentic figure wins for top_p. 0.6 was the PREVIEW family's value and shipped in every release up to 0.0.6.
sampling._why_not_zero: 0.0 is greedy decoding, and greedy is where reasoning models loop: measured 2026-08-07 on a three.js task, the model repeated 'Actually, let me...' inside its reasoning block and never reached the answer. That holds for 0731 as much as for the preview.
sampling._min_p_note: unsloth's docs recommend 0.01 for this model; DeepSeek's own card is silent on it. Sent explicitly because llama.cpp's server default is 0.05 -- not sending it means inheriting a THIRD value nobody chose, the same omission top_p was until #83. Owner approved shipping it 2026-08-10.
sampling._measurement_note: temperature 0 in a probe is a MEASUREMENT decision, not a model default: it buys byte-reproducible output. Those literals stay where they are. And any A/B across the model switch must pin --temperature explicitly on BOTH sides -- the default changed with 0731, and a comparison that inherits it measures the sampling change and the model change in one number.
